plan.notes: Official Greensboro College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Academic Catalog. The catalog publishes degree requirements with no official semester sequence for this program - collected as a single requirements block (requirements_only). This plan covers the major requirements only (Required Courses plus Required Related Courses as printed); Greensboro College requires a minimum of 124 total credit hours for the degree, the balance being general education, all-college/disciplinary requirements and free electives, which are not part of this major block. Where the catalog prints only a block subtotal for a choose-from group, the group is recorded as one choice slot at the printed subtotal with the options named in the choice note; no per-option credits were invented. Catalog pp.217-218. Degree shown as Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in the catalog degree listing. The Department of Political Science and Global Affairs does not offer a concentration within the liberal studies major, as printed.

courses.title: Western Civilizations course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Choose one of these courses, 4 credits as printed: HIS 1150 Western Civilizations I; HIS 1160 Western Civilizations II.

courses.title: History / Politics / Religion courses (choose two)
courses.choice_note: Choose two of these courses, 8 credits as printed: HPS 3120 Revolution; HPS 3360 Nations and Nationalism; HPS 3380 Middle East History, Politics, and Thought; POL 2110 International Relations; POL 2120 Introduction to Comparative Politics; POL 3110 Race and Identity; REP 3100 Theology in Culture and Context.

courses.title: Study Abroad / Experiential course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Choose one of these courses, 2 credits as printed: INT 0001 Study Abroad-Connexion; INT 0002 Study Abroad-Other Programs; HIS/POL/REL 3800 Internship; HIS/POL/REP 3890 Experiential Learning, Global Engagement & Service Learning.

courses.title: Feminist Studies course (choose one)
courses.choice_note: Choose one of these courses, 4 credits as printed: POL 2100 Feminist and Queer Studies; REP 1320 Feminist Ethics and Philosophy.
